reasoning: Stats so far are too small to show clear winners (reach 1-5 per post), so this is an exploration post. Oceans is an untested category from the starting ideas, and 'facts that sound made up' is a new hook shape. I chose a Trial Reel so the experiment reaches non-followers without risking the profile. I also tested two untried settings: documentary music (mystery has been used almost every time) and palette 4 (never used). The reel has 5 short slides to keep watch time high, since past reels had high skip rates. Each slide has one striking highlight number.
topic: Ocean facts: Greenland shark age, Challenger Deep, brine pools, ocean oxygen, unmapped seafloor
hook: Ocean facts that sound made up

slides.title: A 400-year-old shark
slides.body: Greenland sharks may live around 400 years. Some swimming today could be older than the United States.
slides.image_prompt: A huge slow grey shark gliding through dark icy Arctic water, faint light from above, floating ice chunks

slides.title: Everest would vanish
slides.body: The Challenger Deep is about 10,900 m deep. Drop Everest in and its peak stays 2 km underwater.
slides.image_prompt: Cross-section of the ocean with a snowy mountain sunk completely inside a dark trench, deep blue water far above its peak

slides.title: Lakes under the sea
slides.body: In the Gulf of Mexico, super-salty brine pools sit on the seafloor, with their own shores and even waves.
slides.image_prompt: A glossy dark lake on the deep seafloor with a shoreline of mussels, lit by a submarine spotlight in black water
slides.credit: Image courtesy of the NOAA Office of Ocean Exploration and Research. (Public domain) via wikimedia

slides.title: Half your oxygen
slides.body: Tiny ocean plankton make about half the oxygen on Earth. Roughly every other breath comes from the sea.
slides.image_prompt: Glowing green microscopic plankton drifting in sunlit blue water, small oxygen bubbles rising toward the surface
slides.credit: Prof. Gordon T. Taylor, Stony Brook University (Public domain) via wikimedia

slides.title: Mostly unmapped
slides.body: Only about a quarter of the seafloor is mapped in high detail. The rest is still a blur.
slides.image_prompt: A globe of the ocean floor where one small patch is sharp and detailed while the rest fades into blurry dark blue
slides.credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Wanmei Liang, using Landsat data from the U.S.  (Public domain) via wikimedia

cta: Follow for facts you never knew
caption:
The ocean covers about 70% of our planet, yet only about a quarter of its floor is mapped in high detail.

Down there are sharks that may be older than the United States, lakes with their own shores, and a trench deep enough to swallow Mount Everest.

Which of these would you most want to see with your own eyes?
